🔀 Multi-repo context Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts ## Linked repositories findings ### Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts - The agent-memory implementation models revision as append-only suppression, not erasure. Rust `Memory::revise` appends a suppression frame, while `Memory::recall` hides suppressed claims by default and `claims` retains them. There is no inspected `ForgetRequest` or governed-erasure API. (`rust/src/examples/agent_memory.rs:155-290, 396-465`) [::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::] - The Python implementation explicitly documents that revised claims remain present, hash-linked, and recoverable with `include_suppressed=True`; `Memory` is an append-only store. (`python/src/gts/examples/agent_memory.py:3-20, 78-88`) [::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::] - GTS positioning and OKF guidance likewise define agent-memory revision as suppression while preserving original signed history. (`docs/positioning.md:78`; `docs/GTS-OKF.md:136-145`) [::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::] - Compaction carries suppression frames into the rewritten artifact; it is a re-authoring operation, not an in-place governed purge. (`rust/src/compact.rs:330-345, 399-490`) [::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::] - A repository-wide search found no references to the new `ForgetRequest`, `succeedsClaim`, `correctsClaim`, or `retractsClaim` terms. The ontology change therefore has no corresponding transport-level consumer or shared vocabulary implementation in this linked repository. [::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::] The main cross-boundary compatibility point is that consumers using GTS agent memory cannot implement the PR’s physical erasure semantics through the existing suppression-oriented `Memory` workflow; they would need a separate purge/rewrite boundary while preserving the stated append-only behavior for ordinary revision.
